clue.text: Range of knowledge to work on and graduate in

parts.note: to do a job or a room is to work on it
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate's degree
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to a student: get to work and graduate within your chosen field.
explanation.definitionFit: A field or sphere of expertise is a scholar's territory, the area of learning they command.

clue.text: Old and feeble pet cried sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone badly wrong, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: An aged, frail pet whimpers pitifully.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worn out and weakened by age is said to be decrepit.

clue.text: Tate Gallery's craftsman, or TV repairer?

definitions.meaning: a specialist who cleans and repairs old paintings in an art gallery such as London's Tate
a television shows a picture, so whoever mends a set brings the picture back

explanation.surface: Is the expert who mends paintings much different from someone fixing a television?
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a famous London art gallery. The second reading is a joke on 'picture' as the image a TV screen shows.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert who renews damaged artworks is a conservator; fixing a TV set likewise brings back its image.

definitions.meaning: a book, film or piece of music of lasting excellence
the Derby is one of England's five major flat horse races, each called by this name

explanation.surface: A masterpiece is produced at the Derby, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby, run at Epsom, is one of the five English Classics, the most prestigious flat races for three-year-old horses; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A work of enduring, first-rate quality is called this; the five top English flat races share the name.

indicators.note: oddly hints at letters behaving strangely, so the two words are rearranged together

explanation.surface: Two unlike things paired together are delaying something.
explanation.definitionFit: Delaying or postponing a task until later is what a habitual delayer does.

indicators.note: I say tells us the words are to be spoken, so we go by how they sound

parts.note: to stuff something is to fill it

explanation.surface: An exasperated diner told to cram their prime cut somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff it' looks like a rude dismissal, but read it literally as an instruction to fill something; said out loud, those words sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A boneless prime cut such as tenderloin is considered among the choicest steaks.

clue.text: Wife tempted to hold garden party

indicators.note: to hold means the two clue words contain the answer within them, across the word gap

explanation.surface: A wife was tempted to host an outdoor social event.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor fundraising event with stalls and games, typically held in summer.

clue.text: William holds poem to portend bad news

indicators.note: holds means one piece clasps the other within it

parts.note: Bill is a short form of William
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A man named William keeps hold of a gloomy verse foretelling misfortune.
explanation.definitionFit: To augur or foreshadow trouble is to signal that something unfortunate is coming.

indicators.note: captures suggests one piece takes the other prisoner, holding it inside

parts.note: a rider is someone on horseback

explanation.surface: A mounted man seizes a thief.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes a sudden attack to loot is a plunderer or thief.

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
rot is nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Thoughtlessly echoing the usual nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo words without understanding, like a talking bird copying speech.

clue.text: Wrongly named lad close to tear

indicators.note: to tear apart is to rip something up, so these letters are torn and reassembled

explanation.surface: A boy given the wrong name is on the verge of crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tear' looks like a teardrop, but it is the verb meaning rip, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing something by a name it does not really deserve, as in a supposed or alleged thing.

clue.text: Some left at sea during gale-not choosy where they land

parts.note: any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'
on a ship the left-hand side is port
during a gale means in a storm

explanation.surface: Sailors caught out in bad weather will happily put in anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a proverb: in trouble, any refuge will do. 'Some' supplies ANY.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying means that in an emergency one accepts whatever shelter or help is available.

definitions.meaning: a scrap of cloth, a remnant
in Britain, university students hold an annual fundraising week of stunts and parades under this name

explanation.surface: Students drop their fundraising week.
explanation.walkthrough: British universities traditionally hold a 'Rag Week' of fundraising stunts for charity.
explanation.definitionFit: A torn piece of cloth is a remnant; British students' charity fundraising event bears the same name.

definitions.meaning: a unit of guns and the gunners who man them
an electric cell producing current, as in a torch

explanation.surface: Gunners are locked up in a prison cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of big guns and gunners shares its name with a power source for a torch.

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Someone's celebration causes a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuss and bother over something, as in 'much fuss about nothing'.

clue.text: It's odd that it will choke if left in

indicators.note: in tells us that with the letter for left put in, the answer would become the word for choke; so that letter is taken out of it

parts.note: to choke someone is to strangle them

explanation.surface: A strange remark that something will suffocate if it is allowed to stay inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: add L to the answer and you get the word meaning choke, so the answer is that word with L removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something peculiar or unusual is weird or bizarre.

clue.text: Impression very trim from such a seal?

parts.note: an air is an impression or appearance someone gives
tight means close-fitting, very neat and trim

explanation.surface: A good impression comes from a well-trimmed seal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seal' might suggest the animal, but it is a closure that lets nothing through.
explanation.definitionFit: A closure that allows no gas to pass is described as hermetic.

definitions.meaning: leave or permission, as a sailor's shore leave
the colossal copper statue in New York Harbor

explanation.surface: Departing from the famous monument in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Shore leave granted to a sailor is called this, as is the famous statue in New York Harbor.

clue.text: With which judge lets you get your own back

definitions.text: With which judge lets you get your own back

parts.words: With which judge lets you get your own back
parts.note: 'get your own back' reads as revenge, but here means recovering your property: a court ruling that returns premises to their owner

explanation.surface: A court allows you to take revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get your own back' usually means revenge; here it is literal, regaining property such as a house from occupants.
explanation.definitionFit: A court ruling entitling a landlord or lender to retake a property from its occupier.

definitions.meaning: a young ... is an old-fashioned term for a lad

explanation.surface: The barber is just a lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young shaver' is old-fashioned British slang for a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who trims beards is one; old slang also uses it for a young lad.

indicators.note: strangely shows the letters arranged unusually, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recruit signs up without a word.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign up for the armed forces is to enrol as a recruit.

clue.text: Meat to get free? Look into it

indicators.note: into it means the short word goes inside the word just given

parts.note: to escape is to get free
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Instructions on freeing some meat: just examine it.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin boneless slice of veal or other meat, fried in breadcrumbs.

definitions.meaning: cast off, as a snake its skin

explanation.surface: Someone disposed of their garden outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: Casting off as a snake does its skin; also a simple storage hut in a garden.

clue.text: To amuse oneself, start to test weapon

indicators.note: start to means just the first letter of the next word

parts.note: a rifle is a firearm

explanation.surface: For fun, someone tries out a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To toy or play idly with something is to dally or fool about with it.

clue.text: Cut off head of enemy-that's drastic

parts.note: to sever is to cut off

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Beheading an enemy is extreme action.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh and extreme measures are described as harsh or stern.

indicators.note: cut end of means the final letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: Trimming the end off a little container.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal can or container, such as a tea caddy, is called this.

definitions.meaning: someone who welcomes and entertains guests
a great crowd, as in a heavenly throng

explanation.surface: Someone putting on a show for the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A party-giver entertains guests; the word also means a great crowd or army.
